questions.questionHtml: A simple graph is an undirected graph in which each edge connects two different vertices and no two edges connect the same pair of vertices. An “oriented simple graph” is a simple graph which has been converted to a digraph by assigning an orientation to each edge. The orientation of {u,v}{u,v} can be thought of as a mapping of it to either (u,v)(u,v) or (v,u)(v,u) but not to both. Note that if uu and vv are different vertices then the orientation of {u,v}{u,v} is a mapping of it to either (u,v)(u,v) or (v,u)(v,u) but not to both.
